summary: I contrasts eventive fatigue/exertion in Preterit Intransitive with the tired state of Part act. taʕobo, including copular -hat and hatu. Printed taʕibo yo is withheld from firm form claims.
III has either an overt reflexive ruḥo object or an affected person encoded by an l-suffix. Repeated winter ascetic exertion supplies its first Infectum-wa example; no Detransitive is established.
Infectum describes continuing work within a past narrative. Cause and affected participant must not be inferred from the free translation alone.
PrS 66/6: align the German purposive negative with the advice request while preserving affirmative kmatʕabili.
54/75–76: recover the edition’s matching translation for taʕibi iḏoṯi; the supplied German verse stops before it.
115/180: is taʕibo yo a Part act. variant, another state adjective or an edition irregularity? No vowel is normalised.
115/284: resolve taʕəbna as 1pl or 1sg with a resumptive element related to i taʕbe; following ono does not settle the morphology.
Check the clause missing from the supplied corpus Turoyo
rationale: The glossary includes this clause about letting his mare tire, but the supplied Turoyo at 29/167 jumps directly from dlo təʕbo to gšəqli i fərṣa mene. Its German translation nevertheless includes und laß seine Stute müde werden. The citation is correct; the corpus transcription may have omitted the clause. Check the edition before changing the glossary.

summary: Tiring subjects include a head, hands, a horse and rams; participant changes do not establish new senses.
Effort is associated with aʕm- companions/beneficiaries, b- work domains, ʕal persons and qum beneficiaries; none establishes a direct affected object of I.
